claims.text: The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged on this record. The trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry the same trip identifier TRP-00106, and the trace opens at 2026-07-17T08:35:15+08:00, the same pickup event the trip_record records as started_at, so all three admitted artifacts describe one and the same trip.

A route deviation is ESTABLISHED under POL-RD-01 on the governing trace figure. The gps_trace polyline measures 10.78 km (trace_distance_km) against a booked optimal of 7.2 km, an excess of 3.58 km, and both statutory tests pass: 3.58 km is greater than the 0.8 km absolute threshold and 49.72% is greater than the 20% proportional threshold. I cite the trace figure, not the rounded 10.8 km convenience copy on the trip_record, as POL-RD-01 requires.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07. It carries 169 fixes at a 10 second sampling interval over 100% coverage, with no gaps and a max_gap_sec of 0.0, so limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 are not met, no independent corroboration is needed, and the measured excess stands at 3.58 km.

On a METERED fare the rider's remedy is arithmetic under POL-RD-02: recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 7.2 km + 0.28 x 19.0 min) x surge_multiplier 1.0 read from the fare_breakdown + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP on the optimal route = 15.32; refund = 26.04 charged_total less 15.32 = 10.72, rounded up to SGD 10.75. That is 41.17% of the charge, below the 90% full-refund share, so the rider seeks PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 10.75.

The two ERP charges are both off the optimal route: CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) at SGD 3.00 and CTE (Chin Swee Rd tunnel) at SGD 2.50 are each marked on_optimal_route false, and the optimal route carries ERP of 0.00. Under POL-RD-09(1) that SGD 5.50 is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund because the recomputed fare includes only on-optimal-route gantries; it is itemised for transparency but must not be added on top, so the rider's total is 10.75 and not 16.25.

DISCLOSURE: the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00106-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload. Its absence is citable and it defeats any traffic excuse: with no advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses, POL-RD-03 cannot be run on this record, and under POL-RD-13 and POL-RD-08 an uncited external-cause assertion carries no weight and neither reduces the excess nor supplies an amended optimal.

The one chat message is not the detour request POL-RD-04 requires. It was sent by the rider at 08:46:30 reading 'why we at havelock? bugis is behind us' - a contemporaneous objection that the route had left the corridor and was heading away from the destination, not an instruction identifying a waypoint or road. chat_message.waypoint_hint is null, so POL-RD-04(a) to (c) are not met and, per POL-RD-14, the instruction did not cause this excess and no distance is excluded.

POL-RD-05 cannot move the baseline. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are null, so there is no amended optimal to re-apply POL-RD-01 against and the booked 7.2 km optimal stands as the comparator.

This was not a pooled trip, so POL-RD-12 does not substitute any matched-itinerary baseline. The vehicle_type is RYDE_TAXI, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so the 7.2 km booked optimal is the correct and only baseline against which the 3.58 km excess is measured.

No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires and the case should be decided on the money. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, the trace is unimpaired, no timestamps disagree or run backwards, and the computed refund of 10.72 is far below SGD 150.00 and below charged_total. The amount is therefore ripe for a monetary ruling rather than a hold.

I do not press for the POL-RD-06 uplift, and say so honestly: the excess of 49.72% falls just short of the 50% MATERIAL band in POL-RD-01, so the deviation is established but not material and POL-RD-06 limb (b) is not engaged. The driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 96 completed_trips_90d in any event, so no repeat-deviation pattern exists on the citable fields. The rider's correct remedy is the POL-RD-02 partial, not a full refund.

claims.text: Under POL-RD-01 the governing distance is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, not the trip record's rounded copy: 10.78 km against a stored optimal of 7.2 km is an excess of 3.58 km, or 49.72% of optimal. That clears the establishment gates (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km), which the driver does not contest, but it clears neither materiality gate: 49.72% is not greater than 50% of optimal and 3.58 km is not greater than 8.0 km absolute. The deviation is therefore established but NOT material, so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not triggered and the FULL_REFUND uplift needed to support the rider's demand for the whole $26.04 is unavailable on this record.

Where the deviation stands and no exculpatory clause fully excuses it, POL-RD-02 makes the remedy arithmetic rather than discretionary: recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 7.2 optimal km + 0.28 x 19.0 optimal min) x surge 1.0 recorded on the fare breakdown + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP on the optimal route = 15.32. The refund is charged_total 26.04 less 15.32 = 10.72, rounded up to the nearest $0.05, i.e. 10.75. That is a PARTIAL_REFUND of 10.75, which is 41.2% of the charged total and far short of the 90% share that would convert it into a FULL_REFUND under POL-RD-02.

The rider's insistence that the $5.50 of ERP be returned in addition to the distance refund is a double count and is forbidden by POL-RD-09(1). The recomputed fare already includes only gantries lying on the optimal route, and the optimal route carries 0.00 of ERP, so the whole 5.50 of off-route ERP is comprehended inside the 10.72 difference. Adding the ERP line again would produce 16.25 — exactly the arithmetic error POL-RD-09(1) exists to prevent. The ERP is itemised separately for transparency and is not added on top.

Neither ERP line is a phantom charge that could be refunded as a standalone correction under POL-RD-09(4). The CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) gantry is matched by a trace fix at 0.0 m and the CTE (Chin Swee Rd tunnel) gantry by a fix at 24.1 m, both well inside the 250 m match radius, and the fare breakdown carries no airport surcharge at all (0.00), so no billing-integrity defect exists. Nor is POL-RD-09(2) engaged: that limb requires a POL-RD-03 exoneration for an external event, and no such exoneration exists on this record. No standalone pass-through correction is available to the rider.

The driver's profile does not support the repeat-deviation finding POL-RD-06 requires, so none of that clause's three effects can fire. deviation_flags_90d is 0 and completed_trips_90d is 96: the first limb (3 or more flags) fails, and the second limb (a ratio of 0.05 or more with at least 40 completed trips) fails at 0.00. Limbs (a), (b) and (c) — resolution of a balanced case for the rider, the FULL_REFUND uplift, and the conduct referral — are all unavailable, and no other field on either profile may be used to ground an adverse finding against the driver (POL-GEN-01).

Even the reduced figure does not move automatically. The monetary effect of the 10.75 partial refund exceeds the SGD 8.00 execution threshold set on this policy file, so under POL-GEN-05 the ruling is issued but not executed: the amount is held and the case is placed in the human queue for release, where a reviewer confirms execution or converts the matter to review.

Route deviation. The GPS trace EV-GPS-00106 (weight 1.0) measures 10.78 km for this trip. Against the booked optimal of 7.2 km on the trip record EV-TRIP-00106 (weight 1.0), that is an excess of 3.58 km, or 49.72% — above the 20% and 0.8 km establishment gates of POL-RD-01, so a deviation is ESTABLISHED. It stops just short of the 50% and 8.0 km materiality gates, so it is not a MATERIAL deviation: the POL-RD-06 repeat-deviation check and its full-refund uplift are not engaged, and in any event the citable fields show deviation_flags_90d 0 against 96 completed_trips_90d, i.e. no pattern. The trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07 (169 fixes, 10 s sampling, 100% coverage, no gaps), so the measured excess stands and no independent corroboration is needed.

Money. The fare is METERED, so POL-RD-02 applies. recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 7.2 km + 0.28 x 19.0 min) x surge 1.0 read from the fare_breakdown + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP on the optimal route = 15.32. Refund = 26.04 charged_total - 15.32 = 10.72, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 10.75. That is 41.17% of the charge, well below the 90% share that would convert it into a full refund, so the rider's request for the whole 26.04 is not granted and the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 10.75.

Why the $5.50 of ERP is not added on top. Both gantries — CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) SGD 3.00 and CTE (Chin Swee Rd tunnel) SGD 2.50 — are off the optimal route, and the 15.32 recomputed fare already includes only on-optimal-route gantries (0.00 here). POL-RD-09(1) comprehends that ERP inside the 10.72 difference; itemising it separately and adding it would produce 16.25, which is precisely the double count the clause forbids. No standalone pass-through correction is available either: both gantries are matched by trace fixes within the 250 m radius (0.0 m and 24.1 m) and there is no airport surcharge, so POL-RD-09(4) finds no billing-integrity defect.

Why the excess is not reduced. The single chat message EV-CHAT-00106 is the rider's own objection at 08:46:30 — 'why we at havelock? bugis is behind us' — not an instruction, and its waypoint_hint is null, so POL-RD-04 and POL-RD-14 leave the measured excess intact. No pickup or dropoff amendment exists (POL-RD-05), and the vehicle is not pooled (POL-RD-12).

Escalation and process. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown (TRP-00106), the trace is unimpaired, timestamps are consistent, and the refund is far below SGD 150.00. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00106-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0); the claim that discussed it was discarded by the referee and neither side's surviving claims rely on it, so it does not carry this ruling. One procedural note: the monetary effect of SGD 10.75 exceeds the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so under POL-GEN-05 the ruling issues but the amount is held and placed in the human queue for release rather than paid out automatically. Either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties' kept claims converge on the same figures, and the tribunal adopts that common ground.

THE TRIP. Trip TRP-00106 ran from Blk 79 Toa Payoh Central to Bugis Junction on 17 July 2026 and was charged $26.04 on a metered fare. The trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip id TRP-00106 and open at the same pickup event (08:35:15), so the rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged.

DEVIATION. Under POL-RD-01 the governing measurement is gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 10.78 km, not the trip record's rounded 10.8 km convenience copy. Against the booked optimal of 7.2 km this is an excess of 3.58 km, or 49.72% of optimal. Both establishment gates pass (greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20%), so a deviation is ESTABLISHED. Neither materiality gate passes (49.72% is not greater than 50%, and 3.58 km is not greater than 8.0 km), so the deviation is not MATERIAL and the POL-RD-06 uplift is not engaged. The driver's profile shows 0 deviation_flags_90d against 96 completed_trips_90d, so no repeat-deviation pattern exists on the citable fields in any event. The rider's demand for the whole $26.04 is therefore rejected; the correct remedy is the POL-RD-02 partial.

REFUND. The fare is METERED, so the remedy is arithmetic under POL-RD-02: recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 × 7.2 km + 0.28 × 19.0 min) × 1.0 surge (read from the fare_breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP on the optimal route = 15.32. Refund = charged_total 26.04 − 15.32 = 10.72, rounded up to the nearest $0.05 = $10.75. That is 41.2% of the charge, below the 90% share that would convert it to a FULL_REFUND, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of $10.75.

ERP. The $5.50 of ERP (CTE Braddell Rd $3.00, CTE Chin Swee tunnel $2.50) lies off the optimal route, which carries $0.00. Under POL-RD-09(1) that $5.50 is already comprehended inside the $10.72 difference, because the recomputed fare includes only on-optimal-route gantries; adding it again would produce $16.25, the double count POL-RD-09(1) forbids. It is itemised for transparency and is not added on top. Both gantries are matched by the trace (nearest fixes 0.0 m and 24.1 m, inside the 250 m radius) and no airport surcharge was charged, so no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity defect arises and no referral is produced.

NO EXONERATION. The chat log holds one rider message at 08:46:30 ('why we at havelock? bugis is behind us'). It is a contemporaneous objection, not a detour instruction, and waypoint_hint is null, so POL-RD-04 cannot apply and, per POL-RD-14, no distance is excluded. There is no amendment under POL-RD-05 (all amendment fields null) and no pooling under POL-RD-12 (vehicle_type is RYDE_TAXI, solo_optimal_distance_km null), so the booked 7.2 km optimal stands. No traffic advisory covers this window, and no external-cause exoneration under POL-RD-03 was asserted.

ESCALATION. The trace is unimpaired: 169 fixes at 10 s spacing, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap 0.0 — POL-RD-07(a)–(c) are not met, so POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. Trip ids match, timestamps agree, and the refund is far below $150 and below charged_total; no POL-RD-10 trigger fires.

EXECUTION AND APPEAL. The monetary effect of $10.75 exceeds the $8.00 execution threshold on this policy file, so under POL-GEN-05 the ruling issues but is not executed automatically: the amount is held and placed in the human queue for release. Independently of that queue, this is a provisional ruling and either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

CONFIDENCE. The deciding facts rest on the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, all at weight_multiplier 1.0, so confidence is set at 0.90.

ledger.claim: The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged on this record. The trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry the same trip identifier TRP-00106, and the trace opens at 2026-07-17T08:35:15+08:00, the same pickup event the trip_record records as started_at, so all three admitted artifacts describe one and the same trip.

A route deviation is ESTABLISHED under POL-RD-01 on the governing trace figure. The gps_trace polyline measures 10.78 km (trace_distance_km) against a booked optimal of 7.2 km, an excess of 3.58 km, and both statutory tests pass: 3.58 km is greater than the 0.8 km absolute threshold and 49.72% is greater than the 20% proportional threshold. I cite the trace figure, not the rounded 10.8 km convenience copy on the trip_record, as POL-RD-01 requires.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07. It carries 169 fixes at a 10 second sampling interval over 100% coverage, with no gaps and a max_gap_sec of 0.0, so limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 are not met, no independent corroboration is needed, and the measured excess stands at 3.58 km.

On a METERED fare the rider's remedy is arithmetic under POL-RD-02: recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 7.2 km + 0.28 x 19.0 min) x surge_multiplier 1.0 read from the fare_breakdown + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP on the optimal route = 15.32; refund = 26.04 charged_total less 15.32 = 10.72, rounded up to SGD 10.75. That is 41.17% of the charge, below the 90% full-refund share, so the rider seeks PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 10.75.

The two ERP charges are both off the optimal route: CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) at SGD 3.00 and CTE (Chin Swee Rd tunnel) at SGD 2.50 are each marked on_optimal_route false, and the optimal route carries ERP of 0.00. Under POL-RD-09(1) that SGD 5.50 is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund because the recomputed fare includes only on-optimal-route gantries; it is itemised for transparency but must not be added on top, so the rider's total is 10.75 and not 16.25.

Its absence is citable and it defeats any traffic excuse: with no advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses, POL-RD-03 cannot be run on this record, and under POL-RD-13 and POL-RD-08 an uncited external-cause assertion carries no weight and neither reduces the excess nor supplies an amended optimal.

ledger.claim: The one chat message is not the detour request POL-RD-04 requires. It was sent by the rider at 08:46:30 reading 'why we at havelock? bugis is behind us' - a contemporaneous objection that the route had left the corridor and was heading away from the destination, not an instruction identifying a waypoint or road. chat_message.waypoint_hint is null, so POL-RD-04(a) to (c) are not met and, per POL-RD-14, the instruction did not cause this excess and no distance is excluded.

POL-RD-05 cannot move the baseline. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are null, so there is no amended optimal to re-apply POL-RD-01 against and the booked 7.2 km optimal stands as the comparator.

This was not a pooled trip, so POL-RD-12 does not substitute any matched-itinerary baseline. The vehicle_type is RYDE_TAXI, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so the 7.2 km booked optimal is the correct and only baseline against which the 3.58 km excess is measured.

No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires and the case should be decided on the money. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, the trace is unimpaired, no timestamps disagree or run backwards, and the computed refund of 10.72 is far below SGD 150.00 and below charged_total. The amount is therefore ripe for a monetary ruling rather than a hold.

I do not press for the POL-RD-06 uplift, and say so honestly: the excess of 49.72% falls just short of the 50% MATERIAL band in POL-RD-01, so the deviation is established but not material and POL-RD-06 limb (b) is not engaged. The driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 96 completed_trips_90d in any event, so no repeat-deviation pattern exists on the citable fields. The rider's correct remedy is the POL-RD-02 partial, not a full refund.

Under POL-RD-01 the governing distance is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, not the trip record's rounded copy: 10.78 km against a stored optimal of 7.2 km is an excess of 3.58 km, or 49.72% of optimal. That clears the establishment gates (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km), which the driver does not contest, but it clears neither materiality gate: 49.72% is not greater than 50% of optimal and 3.58 km is not greater than 8.0 km absolute. The deviation is therefore established but NOT material, so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not triggered and the FULL_REFUND uplift needed to support the rider's demand for the whole $26.04 is unavailable on this record.

Where the deviation stands and no exculpatory clause fully excuses it, POL-RD-02 makes the remedy arithmetic rather than discretionary: recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 7.2 optimal km + 0.28 x 19.0 optimal min) x surge 1.0 recorded on the fare breakdown + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP on the optimal route = 15.32. The refund is charged_total 26.04 less 15.32 = 10.72, rounded up to the nearest $0.05, i.e. 10.75. That is a PARTIAL_REFUND of 10.75, which is 41.2% of the charged total and far short of the 90% share that would convert it into a FULL_REFUND under POL-RD-02.

The rider's insistence that the $5.50 of ERP be returned in addition to the distance refund is a double count and is forbidden by POL-RD-09(1). The recomputed fare already includes only gantries lying on the optimal route, and the optimal route carries 0.00 of ERP, so the whole 5.50 of off-route ERP is comprehended inside the 10.72 difference. Adding the ERP line again would produce 16.25 — exactly the arithmetic error POL-RD-09(1) exists to prevent. The ERP is itemised separately for transparency and is not added on top.

Neither ERP line is a phantom charge that could be refunded as a standalone correction under POL-RD-09(4). The CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) gantry is matched by a trace fix at 0.0 m and the CTE (Chin Swee Rd tunnel) gantry by a fix at 24.1 m, both well inside the 250 m match radius, and the fare breakdown carries no airport surcharge at all (0.00), so no billing-integrity defect exists. Nor is POL-RD-09(2) engaged: that limb requires a POL-RD-03 exoneration for an external event, and no such exoneration exists on this record. No standalone pass-through correction is available to the rider.

The driver's profile does not support the repeat-deviation finding POL-RD-06 requires, so none of that clause's three effects can fire. deviation_flags_90d is 0 and completed_trips_90d is 96: the first limb (3 or more flags) fails, and the second limb (a ratio of 0.05 or more with at least 40 completed trips) fails at 0.00. Limbs (a), (b) and (c) — resolution of a balanced case for the rider, the FULL_REFUND uplift, and the conduct referral — are all unavailable, and no other field on either profile may be used to ground an adverse finding against the driver (POL-GEN-01).

Even the reduced figure does not move automatically. The monetary effect of the 10.75 partial refund exceeds the SGD 8.00 execution threshold set on this policy file, so under POL-GEN-05 the ruling is issued but not executed: the amount is held and the case is placed in the human queue for release, where a reviewer confirms execution or converts the matter to review.
